subject: Stage 4 labs: persistence changes what 'start of lab' means. Every live cloud lab must (a) open with a clean-start step that clears prior-session resources of the same name, and (b) have its walkthrough exercise the SECOND run, not just the first. Found 2026-07-30 when a leftover lab-vol made 'volume show lab-vol' ambiguous and broke every later step -- would have hit every returning student. Both reviewers had passed the page; the harness caught it.
description:
[2026-07-30 07:52] SHARPENED by Chris 2026-07-30: 'second run' must start from a COMPLETED run, not a crashed one. A successful Cinder run leaves volume in-use + server running; with 1-instance quota that blocks the next attempt. Harness now runs the lab twice with no cleanup between; clean-start step must cover EVERY resource type the lab creates.
[2026-07-31 10:57] Measured 2026-07-31. (b) SATISFIED: all six walkthroughs (cinder/chain/secgroup/neutron/rescue/project) run the lab twice from the prior run's leftovers, and I watched five of them actually do it in green gate runs. (a) audited across all live cloud lab pages: cinder/chain/secgroup/neutron all carry clean-start prose + delete commands; the capstone needs none because its applier is idempotent (check 28) so a re-run creates nothing duplicate. ONE real gap found and fixed: rescue-live is the only lab whose LAUNCH is refused when the project is non-empty (the seed will not overwrite student work), which strands the student -- the terminal they would clean up in is the one that just refused to start. The page warned about the refusal but never said how to resolve it. Added the actionable route: open any other OpenStack lab and use its terminal, with the list/delete commands, plus a caution that the project persists on purpose so deleting is a decision not housekeeping.
[2026-08-02 17:23] [2026-08-02] RE-VERIFIED after I edited six of these harnesses today (exit paths, account-delete removal, capstone baseline clear). My own changes were the risk to this task's guarantees, so I re-measured both halves rather than trusting the 07-31 audit.
(b) RUN-TWICE PROPERTY INTACT: all seven walkthroughs still call runLab twice (chain, cinder, neutron, project, rescue, secgroup, wall). Behavioural proof for one: walkthrough-project ran live today and reported 'WALKTHROUGH PASS: 4/4 twice, second run started from the first run's leftovers' -- twice, on two consecutive runs.
(a) CLEAN-START GUIDANCE INTACT in every live lab. chain-live has a 'Start clean' section explaining the name collision ('the name collides and later commands turn ambiguous') with list -> delete -> WAIT. secgroup-live has 'Start clean, then create the group' with list -> delete -> create. cinder/neutron/rescue carry theirs too. The capstone correctly needs none: its applier is idempotent (check 28), so a re-run creates nothing duplicate.
★ MY FIRST CHECK WAS WRONG AND I CAUGHT IT BY READING THE PAGES. A keyword grep reported chain and secgroup as having ZERO clean-start prose. They both have it -- the grep searched 'clean.start' and the pages say 'Start clean', reversed. Same detector-on-the-wrong-surface pattern as the rest of today; the fix was to look at the content instead of the count.
BOTH (a) AND (b) SATISFIED. Nothing left to build on this task.
